cells.tense: The strength you carry is already pointed at a goal and moving.
cells.act: choose which star to steer by and steer
cells.ask: Give your first hour tomorrow to the aim you are actually headed for, before anything else gets a claim.
cells.core:
You have more in you than most of the people near you can carry, and you have not made a fuss about it. It shows in how things get placed where they are needed, often before anyone asks. Where you are now, that is not only goodwill. There is a heading in it, and the heading came from you.

Put one aim on the line. Tomorrow, take the goal you are already walking toward and give it the first hour of the day. Nothing else gets that slot. No surveying, no re-deciding whether it is the right one. What this does is let the aim be seen from outside. Whoever is being carried starts to see what carries them, and the steering stops being something only you can hold.
cells.sheetLine: You are aiming at something. Name it.
cells.verb: hand the next thing forward before it is asked for
cells.place: where momentum is pointed at a goal and everything is already rolling

cells.tense: This week you are bracing hard enough that the heading has no room left to be chosen.
cells.act: return the small thing you owe before anyone asks
cells.ask: Before anyone has to ask, return the thing you know belongs to another person — an object, an apology, money you borrowed.
cells.core:
You can carry a lot, and you have started carrying it ahead of time. The load has moved into a future that has not arrived, and pushing is now the point. It shows. People get the help before they need it, or get asked a question they cannot answer yet. What was theirs to hold is being handled for them.

Go back to what is already owed. Not the large debt — the lesser one. Hand back the thing you know belongs to someone else before they have to ask. An object, an apology, money you borrowed, credit you took. Doing what is plainly fair sets your feet back down on today. Then the next hand you put out lands where it is actually wanted, not where you guessed it would be needed.
cells.sheetLine: Return what you are holding for someone else.
cells.verb: hand the next thing forward before it is asked for
cells.place: where momentum is pointed at a goal and everything is already rolling

cells.tense: The heading you were following stopped back there, and you have been standing beside it since.
cells.act: drop the wrong approach and keep the commitment
cells.ask: If one way you push at something has gone dead, drop that method and stay with the purpose it was for.
cells.core:
The drive has backed up. You can feel it. What was moving is not moving, and you have gone quiet about that. Strength is still there, but it is not being aimed anywhere, so it drains off through small jobs and short answers. What looked like holding still has become a door you have already walked past.

Test the commitment without the friction of the old method. Take something you have been pushing at in a set way, and put the method down. Keep the purpose. A different route to the same goal, a different hour, a different person to ask, a smaller version of the same move. The test is whether anything at all is still pulling you forward, or only the way you used to do it. The pull returns once you stop wrestling the door.
cells.sheetLine: The direction stopped. The aim has not.
cells.verb: hand the next thing forward before it is asked for
cells.place: where momentum is pointed at a goal and everything is already rolling

cells.tense: You are already pointing at something, and you have been telling people you are still looking.
cells.act: decide the heading from what you want, not from logic
cells.ask: Let your next real choice follow what you want rather than what makes the best sense, and watch what it brings.
cells.core:
There is a heading in you that keeps appearing in what you reach for, who you take seriously, where your money and hours go. Your name for it has been keeping options open. Anyone watching can see where you are pointed. So can you, when nobody is asking.

Let it be decided once without arguing the case first. Take the next real decision and act on what you want, not on what holds up best on paper. Small is fine. Where the free afternoon goes, who you say yes to, which draft you start, which door you let close. If it turns out wrong, you will still know the heading was real, and that is worth more to the next decision than another month of surveying.
cells.sheetLine: You are already pointed. Say the heading.
cells.verb: hand the next thing forward before it is asked for
cells.place: where momentum is pointed at a goal and everything is already rolling
